headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-file and API-mediated interactions can leak data or cascade errors, but no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core is open-source and can read/write data-workflow artifacts, while plano exposes config files and an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven; however, if outputs are manually copied or placed in shared files, prompt-like content could influence plano. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF the operator copies dbt-generated text into plano prompts or config files
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace without content filtering
mitigations: Keep outputs out of prompt text unless reviewed
Separate workspaces for dbt artifacts and plano configs
Use a strict allowlist for any copied snippets
Add a manual review step before feeding agent outputs into plano

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; plano has broad egress and handles logs, traces, and metrics. A plausible pathway exists where warehouse-derived content or operational telemetry is sent onward by plano. The pair lacks documented isolation, so leakage is more than low-risk despite no direct evidence of a shared filesystem.
conditions: IF dbt artifacts containing warehouse data are routed into plano inputs or logs
IF plano forwards telemetry or prompts to external endpoints
mitigations: Redact warehouse fields before handoff
Disable or minimize plano logging for sensitive runs
Route only synthetic samples between tools
Review outbound destinations for both agents
Use separate credentials and workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call data-warehouse APIs and plano can call an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. plano also reports no multiple-instance support, which reduces coordination complexity rather than creating a write conflict. The interaction is plausible but not a default shared-write hazard.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same downstream resource through shared credentials
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable state without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable targets
Serialize any writes through one coordinator
Document ownership of each API scope

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce transformed warehouse outputs that plano may consume through its chat-completions interface. If plano treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade from modeling mistakes into downstream decisions. No verification or critique loop is documented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF plano uses dbt-produced tables, summaries, or text as authoritative input
IF no validation step checks dbt outputs before plano acts on them
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema and freshness checks on dbt outputs
Mark dbt-derived content as untrusted in prompts
Limit plano to advisory-only actions

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no special certifications, residency, or retention commitments, so a concrete compliance mismatch is not documented. The main concern is operational: dbt-core touches warehouse data while plano handles logs and metrics, which could create policy gaps if the operator mixes regulated and non-regulated data. That is a low-risk compliance gap, not a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into plano logs or traces
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees not present in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of logs
Document retention settings for both tools
Use separate environments for sensitive workloads
Review data-processing notices before deployment
